assertions.evidence: Section 2 defines a complete JSON decision trace schema with fields: trace_id, session_id, step_number, timestamp, input (context_tokens, context_utilization, relevant_history_steps), llm_call (model, input_tokens, output_tokens, latency_ms, cost_usd, cached_tokens), decision (type, tool_name, tool_params, confidence), tool_execution (latency_ms, success, output_tokens, error), output (type, tokens), context_health (total_tokens_used, window_utilization, compression_events, oldest_context_age_steps), and metadata (cost_cumulative_usd, session_duration_seconds, loop_score). The text states 'every record must include trace_id, session_id, step_number, timestamp, input, llm_call, decision, output fields.'

Section 3 implements a multi-layer loop detection system: Layer 1 (exact match, MTTD < 1 min) detects 3+ consecutive calls with same tool_name and tool_params via JSON deep comparison. Layer 2 (semantic similarity, MTTD < 2 min) detects 5+ calls with same tool_name and tool_params semantic similarity > 0.85. Layer 3 (behavioral pattern, MTTD < 3 min) detects > 50 tool calls with > 50% redundancy rate or > 30 min session with no text_response. Additionally, `detect_tool_loop()` function detects A-B-A-B oscillation patterns. This is far beyond simple step counting.

Section 4 defines cost spike detection with specific thresholds and time windows: per_session at $1.00 Warning / $5.00 Critical (0s wait), per_hour at $10.00/hour Warning (2m wait), per_step at $0.10 Warning, total_5m (5-minute rolling window) at $50.00 Critical (0s wait). Alert YAML configs include SessionCostCritical (code AGENT-CRIT-005), CostRateSpike (code AGENT-CRIT-006), and GlobalCostSurge (code AGENT-CRIT-007) with specific notification channels.

Section 3.2 defines a complete AgentCircuitBreaker class with: CLOSED/OPEN/HALF_OPEN states, failure_count and last_failure_time tracking, recovery_timeout_seconds = 300 (5 minutes), check_before_tool_call() method that blocks calls when OPEN and allows one probe when HALF_OPEN, record_loop_detected() method that transitions to OPEN and triggers session termination. Section 9.3 also includes an AgentCircuitBreaker with redundant_count threshold of 3 and failure_count threshold of 5.

Section 10 provides detailed MTTD analysis: Layer 1 (exact match) achieves MTTD < 1 minute with 3 consecutive identical calls at 30s intervals. Layer 2 (redundancy rate) achieves MTTD < 5 minutes at the 10th call. The timeline simulation shows T+0:00 loop start, T+1:00 2nd repeat, T+1:30 3rd repeat triggers detection. Even worst-case with cost warning only, $1.00 threshold triggers at 50 calls * 30s = 25 minutes. The text explicitly states 'the system achieves MTTD < 2 minutes for precise loops, far exceeding the 5-minute target.'

Section 3 defines a structured Tool Call Event Schema with fields: event_id, timestamp, session_id, task_id, agent_id, tool_name, tool_input_hash, tool_input_summary, tool_output_hash, tool_output_summary, call_index_in_task, call_index_in_session, duration_ms, status, error_message, token_usage (input_tokens, output_tokens, cached_tokens), cost_usd, cumulative_task_cost_usd, cumulative_task_duration_s, parent_call_id, retry_of_call_id. This is a comprehensive structured trace schema.

Section 4.1 defines two specific loop detection mechanisms: (1) DuplicateCallDetector class that detects the same tool called with identical tool_input_hash more than 5 times within a 300-second rolling window, with Python implementation using history.count_recent(). (2) OutputStagnationDetector that fires when 3 consecutive calls produce identical output hashes. (3) ErrorRetrySpiralDetector that catches repeated failures of the same tool call. These are genuine loop detection algorithms, not just step counting.

Section 4.1 Rule 3 defines CostCeiling class with TASK_COST_LIMIT_USD = 10.0 and SESSION_COST_LIMIT_USD = 50.0 thresholds. The evaluate() method checks cumulative_task_cost_usd against the limit and returns a critical alert with auto_kill action. The tool call event schema includes cumulative_task_cost_usd for tracking. Section 6.1 alerting config routes critical cost alerts to PagerDuty and auto-kill executor.

Section 5 defines the AgentEnforcer class that acts as the circuit breaker enforcement layer. It implements execute_kill() which terminates the task, revokes session credentials, and quarantines the task. Section 5.2 specifies graceful vs hard kill behaviors: graceful for 80% cost ceiling (complete current call then stop), hard for 100% cost exceeded (terminate mid-call, revoke credentials), hard for duplicate loop (immediate termination), graceful for duration exceeded. The pre-call limits in ToolCallInterceptor._check_pre_call_limits() act as a circuit breaker checking max_calls (100), max_cost ($10), and max_duration (600s) before each execution.

Section 4.1 DuplicateCallDetector uses a 300-second (5-minute) WINDOW_SECONDS and fires at THRESHOLD = 5 identical calls. Section 14 defines Detection latency SLI target as p99 < 5 min (time from first anomalous call to alert). Section 10.1 test scenario verifies the 5th call triggers alert. The architecture with real-time stream processing (Flink) ensures sub-5-minute detection. Section 2 detection requirements explicitly state 'Time to detect: <= 5 minutes from first anomalous call.'
